seed.proposition_text:
The terminal source of the epileptogenesis premise states that Wwox knockout MICE have no reported epileptic seizures, which contradicts rather than supports the claim five LEGEND surfaces trace to it.
The absence of epilepsy in the mouse is treated by these authors as an open discrepancy with a candidate explanation, not as an oversight, which makes the rat-to-mouse transfer a question rather than an assumption.
The behavioural contrast is stated a third time and extended to motor phenotype, so the species difference is a deliberate, repeated claim of this paper.
The rat lde allele, though a C-terminal frameshift rather than a deletion of the locus, behaves as a protein-level functional null in the two tissues assayed — which refines the allele-class caution recorded on 2026-08-06 from PMID 19936220.
Transcript level is unaffected, so the loss is post-transcriptional and cannot be explained by nonsense-mediated decay of the mutant message.
The antibody epitope lies outside the region altered by the mutation, so the absent Western signal means absent protein rather than a masked epitope. This is the control that makes the functional-null conclusion admissible.
The mechanism proposed for the protein's disappearance is asserted, not measured: no turnover assay, no inhibitor and no route determination appears anywhere in the paper.
Audiogenic seizure penetrance is 95 percent, and the denominator is 20 animals after exclusions rather than the 23 initially exposed.
Latency to seizure shortens across repeated daily stimulations, a kindling-like progression rather than a fixed trait threshold.
No control animal seized under identical stimulation, which bounds the phenotype to genotype rather than to the stimulus.
Spontaneous seizure incidence measured first-hand in this paper's backcross cohort is 60 percent, roughly double the 33 percent the authors cite from their own earlier strain.
Epileptiform activity is documented electrographically and not only behaviourally, and it is present in every mutant even without stimulation.
The EEG cohort is very small and sex-mixed, which bounds the electrographic result to a demonstration rather than a quantified prevalence.
The paper explicitly excludes a systemic metabolic cause for the rat's hyperexcitability — the strongest single statement it makes about mechanism, and one that rests entirely on an unread source.
The mouse null's lethality is attributed here to a severe serum abnormality, independently corroborating the measured systemic decompensation recorded from PMID 19936220 on the same day.
The rat is asserted to lack that metabolic derangement, which is what would make the two models a natural dissociation of seizures from systemic illness — if the assertion holds.
The rat survives substantially longer than the mouse null, which is the material fact behind the 'the mice may die first' explanation for the absent mouse epilepsy.
Heterozygotes are phenotypically normal in the rat as in the mouse, converging on the absence of a haploinsufficiency phenotype in rodents.
Heterozygote protein is measurably reduced without any phenotype, so a partial reduction in Wwox protein is tolerated in rat tissue.
The rat reproduces the mouse's relative brain enlargement, which is brain sparing during wasting in both species and must not be read as brain overgrowth in either.
The anatomical lesion is fully penetrant in hippocampus and partial in amygdala, with clean controls — the structural correlate the mouse literature lacks.
The regional restriction of the vacuolation is itself unusual among genetic epilepsy models, which is what makes it mechanistically interesting rather than incidental degeneration.
The rat develops no tumours, adding a third genotype to the contested picture of WWOX-loss tumorigenesis in rodents.
The rat's bone and calcium phenotype is milder than the mouse's, so the skeletal severity is not a conserved consequence of Wwox loss.
The headline 95 percent audiogenic penetrance was measured in females only, a restriction stated in the figure and absent from the Results narrative and the abstract.
The Western blot shows complete absence of both Wwox species in mutant tissue, with heterozygote lanes visibly intermediate.
The Figure 1 caption assigns its panels to the wrong genotypes, so anyone reading the caption without the image will invert which hippocampus is normal.
Interictal spikes are visible as discrete marked events in the mutant trace and absent in the control trace, supporting the text's claim at the level of the raw record.
Table 2 formalises the species difference: the Epilepsy row is populated for the rat alone and is empty for both mouse models, which is the single clearest refutation of the imported premise.
The same table records the viability gap that underwrites the authors' explanation for why the mouse may never be observed to seize.

The pixel side: Fig 1G's three construct headers read Wwox, WWY33R, WWY61R across nine lanes. No Y34.
The Discussion cites `Fig. 3D` twice — for the ΔNp73 apoptosis result and for the increased apoptotic activity — and FIG 3 HAS NO PANEL D. Its caption declares A, B and C only, and the image carries exactly three panels. The data meant are in Fig 3C. A dangling internal cross-reference, twice, in the paragraph that carries the paper's central interpretive move.
🔴 'SIGNIFICANTLY' IS USED WITH NO STATISTIC ANYWHERE IN THE PAPER, AND FIG 3A HAS NO ERROR BARS. The caption says the luciferase results are the average of three experiments; the panel shows twelve bars with ZERO dispersion indicators, while Fig 3C — from the same paper, same figure — does carry error bars and an explicit `average ± SD`. The screen over the whole body finds `P <`, `P =`, `P<` and `P=` at ZERO occurrences: no test, no threshold, no n per condition. The dose-dependence and the suppression are visible as a trend; 'significantly' is a word here, not a result.
The pixel side, plus a second defect the text does not cause: Fig 3A carries no error bars on any of its twelve bars, and its y-axis is MISLABELLED. The axis reads `% of Luciferase (10³)` while the caption defines the values as fold induction over empty vector — and bar 1 is printed as 1.0, which is a fold and not a percentage. The printed bar values (1.0, 497, 1.7, 3.7, 2.7, 339, 63, 1481, 2062, 996, 303, 3366) are fold inductions on an axis claiming percent-times-a-thousand. Same class as the Z-score-printed-as-fold found in Liu 2018: a units label that would mislead anyone reading the panel without the caption.
🔴 COLOCALISATION IS ASSERTED WITHOUT A MERGED IMAGE, AND THE ASYMMETRY RUNS AGAINST THE CLAIM. Fig 2A shows each condition as two separate single-channel images side by side (c1/c2, d1/d2, e1/e2) — there is no overlay panel anywhere in Fig 2A, so 'colocalization' is inferred from two images and not shown in one. In Fig 2B the pattern inverts in the least helpful direction: the NEGATIVE conditions (i = p73γ, j = p73βY487A, k = p53) ARE displayed as two-colour merged images, while the POSITIVE ones (g = p73α, h = ΔNp73) are displayed as separate channels. The panels that would benefit most from an overlay are the ones that do not get one.
The pixel side: Fig 2A c1/c2, d1/d2 and e1/e2 are single-channel pairs with no overlay; Fig 2B i, j and k are two-colour merges while g and h are single-channel pairs.
THE ROUTING RESULT IS AN OVEREXPRESSION RESULT AND THE AUTHORS SAY SO IN THE DISCUSSION. This is the single most important qualification for a model that carries the routing principle as architecture: the redistribution of p73 is what OVEREXPRESSED Wwox does. The endogenous support is real but narrower — Fig 1B (etoposide-treated 293), Fig 1F and Fig 2B (MCF-7 endogenous Wwox), Fig 2C/D (siRNA knockdown) — and the endogenous localisation result is reported as 'more than 50% of MCF-7 cells' with no n and no test.
The endogenous localisation figure is a bare proportion: no denominator, no field count, no statistic.
🔴 THE DOSE-DEPENDENCE OF THE RELOCALISATION — THE STRONGEST FORM OF THE ROUTING EVIDENCE — IS IN A FIGURE THIS READING COULD NOT OPEN. Less Wwox giving more nuclear p73 is the closest thing in the paper to a causal titration, and it lives in supplementary Fig 5, behind PMC's proof-of-work. The claim is therefore carried here at the level the accessible panels support (Fig 2A, categorical, overexpression) and NOT at the level the text implies.
🔴 THE CONTROL THAT MAKES FIG 3B INTERPRETABLE IS ALSO IN AN UNOPENABLE FIGURE. Fig 3B compares p21 levels across Wwox and WWY33R conditions; whether Wwox and WWY33R were expressed comparably is the difference between a functional result and an expression artefact, and that control is supplementary Fig 6. Without it, the p21 restoration by WWY33R cannot be separated from a difference in how much protein each construct made.
THE Y33 RATIONALE IS INHERITED FROM A PAPER THIS CORPUS DOES NOT HOLD. Y33 was chosen for study because Chang et al. reported it affects murine Wox1's interaction with JNK; the same reference supplies the claim that altering Y33 reduces Wwox's proapoptotic activity. That reference is J Biol Chem 278:9195-9202 (2003) = PMID 12514174, already known to this corpus as MISSING FROM DISK AND UNREAD. PREMISE: DATO in the source, but a DATO we have never verified — the load-bearing premise under the whole Y33 story is a paper we do not have.
A NEGATIVE PANEL, AND IT IS TREATED AS ONE. The p53 non-interaction is a genuine and useful result — it is what makes the PPPPY-motif explanation specific rather than decorative — but Fig 1C is a negative panel and, per the standing correction, a negative panel does not by itself permit a comparison normalised for bait quantity. The authors' own framing is appropriately modal ('perhaps explaining'), and that modal is worth preserving on the way out.
THE APOPTOSIS RESULT CONTAINS ITS OWN TENSION AND THE AUTHORS FLAG IT AS A GUESS. WWY33R does not bind p73, yet WWY33R + p73β gives the LARGEST apoptotic population in Fig 3C (~38%, above WT-Wwox + p73β at ~31%). The explanation offered is explicitly one possibility among others, not a demonstration. Anyone carrying 'Wwox-p73 cytoplasmic cooperation drives apoptosis' out of this paper must also carry the fact that the non-binding mutant produced more apoptosis than the binder.
A LABELLING HAZARD FOR ANYONE TRANSPORTING FIG 3C. The panel labels the amino-terminally truncated p73 isoform as `DN-p73`, while the same paper uses `DN-Src` to mean DOMINANT-NEGATIVE Src. In Fig 3C `DN-p73` means ΔNp73 — a deletion variant — not a dominant-negative construct, and the two senses of `DN` sit in adjacent figures. Recorded because the misreading is silent and would invert the interpretation of the ΔNp73 bars.
The pixel side of the p53 negative: Fig 1C is a two-blot negative panel — anti-p53 shows p53 in the p53 immunoprecipitate, anti-Myc shows Wwox in the Myc immunoprecipitate, and neither protein appears in the other's lane. It is a clean absence, and an absence is all it is: with no input blot the panel carries no normalisation for how much bait was present in each arm.
The pixel side of the apoptosis tension: reading the Fig 3C bar heights against its axis gives empty vector ~7.5%, Wwox ~16.5%, p73β ~14%, Wwox+p73β ~31%, ΔNp73 ~8%, Wwox+ΔNp73 ~26.5%, WWY33R ~11%, WWY33R+p73β ~38%, WWY33R+ΔNp73 ~12.5%. THE NON-BINDING MUTANT PLUS p73β IS THE TALLEST BAR IN THE PANEL. Error bars are present here, unlike Fig 3A. The panel also labels ΔNp73 as `DN-p73`, two figures away from a `DN-Src` that means dominant-negative. AND THE PANEL COUNT ITSELF: Fig 3 carries exactly three panels — A (luciferase), B (blots), C (these bars). There is no panel D anywhere in the image, which is what makes the Discussion's two `Fig. 3D` citations dangling.
The paper's only GRADED-DOSE titration of Wwox against p73 localisation displays neither of the two things it is cited for. The panel carries no dose labels of any kind — the amounts of Myc-Wwox the text says were varied appear nowhere on the figure — there is no merged channel anywhere (Wwox and p73 are shown as separate single channels b1/b2 and c1/c2, the same absence already recorded for Fig 2A), and no cell count, n or statistic appears on it, although the proposition it supports is explicitly about a PROPORTION of cells ('some cells'). ⚠️ TWO SCOPE LIMITS, BOTH ADDED BY THE BLIND AUDIT AND BOTH KEPT: (1) 'only titration' is precise only for a graded dose series — Fig 2 C/D is an siRNA knockdown of endogenous Wwox read out on p73 localisation, i.e. a second Wwox-level-versus-localisation experiment by a different means. (2) The supporting-figure LEGENDS are not in the retrieved artifact set (the caption stubs returned HTTP 403), so 'no dose labels ON THE FIGURE' must NOT be read as 'the doses are unstated in the supplement'. The absence is established of the image, not of the supplement.
MEASURED, and it does not show the step it is cited for — but only ONE of the three measures I first reported survives adversarial re-measurement, and the other two are withdrawn. ROBUST: the Wwox-positive AREA of the reduced-dose field c1 is not lower than the higher-dose field b1 (my 6.04% vs 4.70%; one auditor reproduces the direction in 27 of 27 bound/threshold configurations, the other measures 3.74-5.38% vs 3.47-4.98% — same direction, different absolute values). WITHDRAWN: 'on any measure', and with it the 99th-percentile pair 255 vs 237, which does not reproduce — one auditor obtains 239.0 vs 241.2 (reversing the direction) and the other obtains 255 for BOTH fields; three measurements, three different answers, so the statistic is windowing-dependent and cannot carry a finding. Also withdrawn: the mean-of-positive-pixels gap, reported by both auditors as parity rather than 173.3 vs 160.8. ⚠️ AND THE DIRECTION RESTS ON AN ASSUMPTION THAT MUST BE DECLARED: Fig 5 has NO CAPTION in either HTML or PDF — only the citing sentence's parenthetical 'b vs. c'. Nothing in the paper states which of b and c is the reduced dose. The reading c = reduced is the natural one and it is an assumption, not a datum. What survives: the figure cannot support the asserted decrease in Wwox expression, in either direction.
CORRECTED BY THE BLIND AUDIT, AND THE CORRECTION MAKES THE FINDING STRONGER, NOT WEAKER. WITHDRAWN: 'both p73 panels contain both morphologies' — only the b2 half was ever established. WHAT STANDS, confirmed independently by both auditors: the high-Wwox field b2 contains BOTH a solid nuclear-pattern ellipse (a run of 13-15 consecutive pixels at 193-199 across its middle) AND a ring with a dark centre, side by side in one field; and the reduced-Wwox field c2 contains a cell whose horizontal profile at row 61 runs bright-dark-bright (113 -> 54 -> 201), which both auditors reproduced EXACTLY. WHAT CHANGES: c2 is ring-DOMINATED — one auditor finds zero compact objects in it above a green threshold of 140 and its largest object a ring — so c2 does not carry the nuclear morphology at all. THE CONSEQUENCE RUNS AGAINST THE TEXT: the field cited to show 'retention of p73 in the nucleus of some cells' is the field in which the nuclear pattern is hardest to find, while the field cited for cytoplasmic sequestration contains a nuclear-looking cell. ⚠️ ABSOLUTE RATIOS ARE METHOD-DEPENDENT AND ARE NOT A FINDING: my panel-a range 1.08-1.14 does not reproduce (one auditor 1.038-1.069, the other 1.01-1.05). Only the COMPARISON — b2's solid ellipse falls inside panel a's nuclear range, whatever that range is measured to be — is stable across all three measurements.
🔴 THE HEADLINE NUMBER I FIRST REPORTED WAS AN ARTEFACT OF MY OWN UNSTATED MEASUREMENT WINDOW, AND IT IS WITHDRAWN. I originally reported WT/mutant Wwox-to-tubulin ratios of 1.09 / 1.39 / 0.82 and called them 'straddling unity'. Re-measured under three windows: NARROW (my original) 1.07 / 1.32 / 0.70; WIDE 1.13 / 1.36 / 1.20; FULL BOX 1.11 / 1.43 / 1.07. THE FIRST TWO PAIRS ARE STABLE — WT is expressed 1.07-1.43x the mutant at 0 and 10 ng p73b under every window. THE THIRD PAIR IS NOT MEASURABLE: it swings from 0.70 to 1.20 depending on the integration window, so 'the mutant exceeds WT at 50 ng' is a property of my window and not of the blot. WITHDRAWN: 'straddling unity' and 'not systematically over- or under-expressed'. WHAT SURVIVES, AND IS STRENGTHENED: under every robust measurement the mutant is expressed AT OR BELOW wild type, so the Fig 3B result that WWY33R restores p21 CANNOT be attributed to more mutant protein being present. That is what the control was for, and it holds more firmly on the corrected numbers than on mine. ⚠️ My densitometry, not a reported result: the paper performs no densitometry, states no replicate count for this blot and prints no statistic on it.
🔴 WITHDRAWN IN FULL BY THE BLIND AUDIT — AND IT WAS THE MOST ATTRACTIVE FINDING IN THIS READING, WHICH IS WHY IT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN DELETED. I claimed that Fig 6 supplies the dose-to-expression step Fig 5's citing sentence asserts and does not display, calling it a cross-panel rescue within the same supplement. IT FAILS ON CELL LINE, and I verified this against the body myself rather than on the auditor's word: Fig 5 is NIH 3T3 ('we transfected NIH 3T3 with equal amounts of HA-p73b and different quantities of Myc-Wwox'), while Fig 6 belongs to the SAOS-2 p21/transactivation series. Two different cell lines: Fig 6 CANNOT establish the dose-to-expression step for Fig 5's experiment. Also corrected: 'roughly 1.6-fold protein for 2-fold plasmid' is wrong — the per-level folds are approximately 4.0 / 1.3 / 1.5, and the 0 ng pair is greater than 2x, not 1.6x; and 'monotonically' is vacuous over two dose points. WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND MUCH NARROWER: Fig 6 carries a labelled dose axis that Fig 5 lacks, and within the SAOS-2 series plasmid dose does raise Wwox protein. The gap in Fig 5's sentence is NOT closed anywhere in this paper.
Lane 1 of Fig 6 (no Wwox, no WWY33R, no p73b) carries essentially no Wwox signal against every transfected lane: no detectable Wwox at this exposure. ⚠️ THE BARE NUMBER IS WITHDRAWN AS METHOD-DEPENDENT — I reported a Wwox-to-tubulin ratio of 0.071 and the auditors obtain 0.062 unsubtracted, 0.015 background-subtracted, and 0.160 under a different lane geometry, a spread of 0.001 to 0.19. What is stable is the comparison: lane 1's Wwox integrated density is under 10% of a transfected lane's on every method tried. ⚠️ AND THE CELL-LINE ATTRIBUTION IS THE BODY'S, NOT THE PIXELS': Fig 6's cell line is NEVER STATED in the retrieved artifact, because the supporting-figure legends are absent, so identifying this blot as SAOS-2 is an inference from the surrounding text and is declared as one. The body says SAOS-2 'express very low levels of Wwox' — LOW, not none, and the panel is consistent with either.
FAIRNESS RECORDED AGAINST MY OWN READING, TWICE OVER. I originally wrote that lane 10's tubulin is 'lowest by a wide margin' and that lane 10 is 'the single matched pair in which WWY33R appears to exceed wild-type'. THE SECOND HALF IS WITHDRAWN — see entries[28]: that apparent excess is a property of my integration window, not of the blot. THE FIRST HALF IS NARROWED: lane 10's tubulin is the lowest of the ten under every window I tested, but the MAGNITUDE is severely window-dependent — a 55% deficit against the next-lowest lane in my narrow window, and only about 5-10% in a wide one. ⚠️ ONE AUDITOR'S PROPOSED MECHANISM DOES NOT REPRODUCE AND IS RECORDED AS REJECTED: it attributed the effect to lane 10's tubulin band sloping upward and exiting the row window, band centre at row 146 against 148-154 elsewhere. Measured directly, lane 10's darkness-weighted band centroid is 155.75 and the ten lanes span 154.30-157.40 — lane 10 is inside the window and is not an outlier in position. The window sensitivity is real; that explanation of it is not.
The nine DNA-content histograms of Fig 7, which are the raw data behind the Fig 3C sub-G1 quantification, are NOT ON A COMMON SCALE: reading the printed y-axis maxima in panel order they are 148, 72, 88, 60, 132, 64, 124, 60, 120 — eight distinct values across nine panels, with 60 shared by panels 4 and 8. CORRECTED WORDING: I first wrote that each panel is scaled to a DIFFERENT maximum, which my own list contradicts, and both auditors caught it. THE READING OF THE DIGITS WAS ITSELF CONTESTED AND I ADJUDICATED IT FROM THE PIXELS: one auditor read panels 4, 8 and 9 as 68, 68 and 128; the other reproduced 60, 60 and 120 exactly. Re-rendered upright at 26x, the disputed glyph has an open centre and no waist, unlike the plainly waisted 8 of the 148 in panel 1 — it is a zero, and 60/60/120 stands. The consequence either way is unchanged: the height of a sub-G1 peak is not comparable between panels by eye.
No sub-G1 gate marker is drawn on any of the nine panels of Fig 7, and no percentage is printed on any of them. The figure therefore does not display the gating that produced the percentages plotted in Fig 3C: the reader is shown the distributions and not the region that was counted, so Fig 3C's numbers cannot be checked against Fig 7 by any means available in the paper. Verified exhaustively rather than by eye — one auditor resolved each panel interior into connected components and found a single dark trace carrying 100% of the ink in each, with no gate line, region bar or printed figure anywhere. ⚠️ SCOPE: the supporting-figure legends are absent from the retrieved artifact set, so this establishes that the gating is not shown ON THE FIGURE, not that gating detail is absent from the supplement.
🔴 STATED SO IT CANNOT BE MISREAD AS AN ACCUSATION. The four Fig 7 panels with the lowest y-maxima (60, 60, 64, 72 — Wwox+p73b, WWY33R+p73b, dNp73+Wwox, Wwox) are exactly the four conditions Fig 3C reports as most apoptotic; one auditor measured the Fig 3C bar heights independently and returned the identical set, with ranks 3 through 9 matching as well. That correlation is what GENUINE apoptosis would produce, because a depleted G1 peak lowers the auto-scale; it is recorded as a confound in the DISPLAY and explicitly NOT as evidence of manipulation. The consequence is only that the eye cannot be used here, and Fig 3C's own average +/- SD from three experiments — which the caption does report — remains the quantification that carries the result.
🔴 THE FINDING THAT NARROWS  , AN ABSENCE MADE MACHINE-CHECKABLE — AND THE AUDIT MADE IT STRONGER BY CORRECTING MY COUNT UPWARD. The authors' own scope for the phosphorylation result is the INTERACTION and nothing more: Y33 phosphorylation is said to regulate the Wwox-p73 interaction. I first reported that EIGHT sentences mention Src; both auditors independently measured TWENTY (29 occurrences document-wide), and my figure was wrong. THE SUBSTANTIVE FINDING IS UNAFFECTED AND HOLDS OVER THE LARGER SET: ZERO of those twenty sentences also mentions localisation, cytoplasm, nucleus, redistribution or sequestration, confirmed by both auditors including one running a plus-or-minus 400-character proximity screen whose only near-misses are adjacent sentences. No experiment in this paper manipulates phosphorylation and measures where p73 goes: Fig 4 is entirely binding and phospho-blot biochemistry, while Fig 2 and Fig 5 are localisation with no Src arm. 'Phosphorylation-dependent subcellular rerouting' is therefore a CONJUNCTION of two separately supported legs and not a relation this paper tests.
The two Discussion sentences that carry the 'cytoplasmic cooperation drives apoptosis' leg BOTH cite a panel that does not exist. Fig 3's caption declares panels (A), (B) and (C) and the image carries three panels; the Discussion cites 'Fig. 3 D' twice, once for the ΔNp73 result and once for the increased apoptotic activity. The data meant are in Fig 3C, so this is a citation defect and not a missing experiment — but the leg of the argument that a downstream reader would follow terminates, twice, at a label with nothing behind it.
The sentence that sends the reader to Fig 7 for the sub-G1 apoptosis result. It is the text side of the three Fig 7 attestations that follow it in this manifest: what Fig 7 is cited to show is that Wwox or p73β alone raises the sub-G1 fraction over empty vector, a comparison of MAGNITUDES between panels.

The Results section heading asserts that p100/p52 knockout PREVENTS tumorigenesis, while the paragraph beneath it reports that only 10% of the knockout mice remained tumour-free - i.e. roughly 90% developed tumours, and the effect is a delay of onset, not prevention.
The paper's own paragraph gives the numbers that make the heading above an overstatement: tumour onset in the knockout is delayed to 24 weeks and 10% remain tumour-free at 52 weeks, so about 90% of Tax+ p100-/- mice did develop tumours.
The Discussion states the same result accurately as a REDUCTION, so the overstatement is confined to the Results heading and the paper contradicts it itself. This is what makes the finding a surface defect rather than a disagreement about the biology.
VISUAL ATTESTATION - the Kaplan-Meier curve confirms delay rather than prevention, and gives the shape the prose does not: the knockout curve falls steeply from ~22 weeks and plateaus at 10% tumour-free from ~34 weeks through the end of observation, while the Tax+ p100+/+ curve reaches 0% tumour-free by ~24-25 weeks.
The figure caption names a single control-group size for both Tax-negative genotypes together, which is the statement the panel's own legend qualifies.
VISUAL ATTESTATION - the in-panel legend prints n=9 for EACH of the two Tax-negative control groups, whereas the caption names 'Tax-free p100+/+ or p100-/- mice (n = 9)', which reads as nine control animals in total rather than eighteen. The control-arm size differs between the caption and the figure's own legend.
The rescue conclusion - that re-expressed p100, and p52 alone, restore Tax-driven transformation - is the claim the unmarked bars of Figure 1C have to carry.
VISUAL ATTESTATION - in Figure 1C the two arms that FALL carry significance marks while the two rescue arms that RISE carry none. The rescue conclusion is therefore statistically unmarked at n=3. Stated as absence of a drawn marker, NOT as a difference tested and found absent.
The text claims that loss of p100/p52 produces almost COMPLETE recovery of WWOX from Tax-mediated repression.
VISUAL ATTESTATION - Figure 2B's own printed percentiles refute 'almost complete recovery': in the p100-knockout background Tax still lowers wwox from 94 to 63, a residual repression of about a third. Recovery is substantial and partial, not almost complete. The paper's section heading, which says 'largely dependent', is the accurate surface.
The paper states that WWOX repression in HTLV-I-transformed and ATL lines is stronger at the protein level than at the mRNA level - a post-transcriptional component to WWOX loss.
VISUAL ATTESTATION - WWOX protein is lower than WWOX mRNA in every one of the six virus-positive lines, and the panels carry numbers the running text does not. CAVEAT CARRIED WITH IT: 2E is normalised to β-actin and 2F to Hsp90, they are single runs, and neither panel carries a significance mark, so this is a consistent direction across six lines and not a tested dissociation.
The proposed mechanism for the protein-level loss - ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation with BOTH a Tax-dependent and a Tax-independent arm - is asserted partly on data that were not shown.
VISUAL ATTESTATION - Figure 6D, the panel cited in support, contains NO Tax-negative condition: Tax is present in all nine lanes. The panel can therefore establish that WWOX is proteasomally degraded, but cannot separate a Tax-dependent from a Tax-independent arm, and the Tax-INDEPENDENT half of the claim rests entirely on the unshown data.
The paper's only clinical anchor: WWOX is reported as significantly decreased in about 78% of primary ATL patient samples.
VISUAL ATTESTATION - Figure 2G carries NO significance mark of any kind, on any bar, although the sentence citing it says 'significantly decreased'. The comparator is a single healthy donor set to 100 while the other two controls sit at 117 and 149, and one of the two unreduced patients (#2) has an error bar reaching the comparator.
The paper's pathophysiologic conclusion for primary patient material - the step from cell lines to human disease - and the sentence the uncited supplement bears on.
🔴 THE CLINICAL CLAIM'S MISSING MEASUREMENT. The only viral transcript ever measured in the ATL patients is HBZ, in the uncited supplemental Figure S3; Tax itself is never measured in patient material. ⚠️ STATED AS AN ASSUMPTION, NOT A FACT: the cross-read below assumes that 'ATL #1-#9' denotes the same patients in the same order in Figure 2G and in Figure S3. NOTHING in either caption, the figures or the Methods asserts that. On that assumption WWOX does not track HBZ; without it, only the absence of any Tax measurement stands.
Supplemental Figure S3's own caption confirms what it measures and in which subjects - HBZ transcript in the ATL patients and controls - which is what makes its absence from the main text a gap rather than a mislabelling.
The specificity control for the whole NF-kB argument: WWOX does not inhibit TNFa-induced NF-kB, so its effect is Tax-selective rather than a general suppression of the reporter. A genuine and well-placed negative.
The text describes the Y33R mutant as DRAMATICALLY enhancing Tax oncogenicity.
VISUAL ATTESTATION - the word 'dramatically' is attached to the WEAKER and less significant of the two effects. In both the colony and the tumour-weight panels the Y33R increase is about +28% at a single asterisk, while the wild-type suppression is about -60% at two asterisks.
The text asserts an inverse correlation between Tax-induced NF-kB activity and WWOX knockdown efficiency. The separate dose-dependence claim is carried by a different sentence and is not quoted here.
VISUAL ATTESTATION - Figure 5 carries NO significance mark in ANY of its four panels, so every dose-dependence and correlation claim resting on it is statistically unmarked. In Figure 5C the Y33R error bars reach below the control level, so the Y33R increase in MT-2 cells is not separable from the comparator by inspection.
The statistical apparatus for the whole paper is a two-tailed Student t test between two groups, with no correction for multiplicity declared anywhere despite repeated multi-arm comparisons.
🔴 THE FIRST LEG OF WHAT BEARS ON  . Y33R retains Tax binding, so for this partner Y33 is not the determinant of binding; the paper generalises to a WW-domain-independent binding activity. TWO LIMITS CARRIED: the confirmatory WW-deletion experiment is 'data not shown', and the generalising sentence also cites reference 42, so the conclusion does not rest on the unshown deletion alone.

🔴 CORRECTED AFTER A BLIND LOCATOR AUDIT, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE POINT. The authors ASSERT that WWOX does not affect Tax subcellular localisation. It therefore may NOT be used to exclude the relocalisation route of   - the exclusion is unresolved in this paper, not demonstrated.

The third route this paper supplies, and the one   does not name: WWOX acts by blocking a third protein's recruitment to a partner, not by binding strength and not by relocalisation.
The authors' wording is hedged on the mutant's gain-of-function and unhedged on the wild type. Wild-type WWOX returns IKKa-RelA association to the Tax-negative baseline rather than abolishing it, so 'completely prevented' is correct for the TAX-MEDIATED increment and must not be carried forward as abolition of the interaction. Inputs are controlled: WWOX WT and Y33R are expressed comparably and Tax is not lower in the WWOX lane.
🔴 ADDED AFTER A BLIND LOCATOR AUDIT FOUND IT, AND IT IS A HARDER INTERNAL CONTRADICTION THAN THE SECTION HEADING. The paper states that ALL Tax+ p100+/+ mice had tumours by 18 weeks of age, citing Figure 1A - and Figure 1A shows about 41% of them still tumour-free at 18 weeks, reaching 0% only at about 25 weeks.
VISUAL ATTESTATION - the Tax+ p100+/+ Kaplan-Meier curve read point by point refutes 'all the mice had tumors by 18 weeks of age'. At 18 weeks roughly 41% of that cohort is still tumour-free; the curve does not reach 0% until about 25 weeks.

seed.proposition_text:
The central positive result: hepatocyte-specific Wwox deletion raises HIF1alpha occupancy on its own glycolytic target promoters. This is the third side of the hepatic triangle and it holds.
Fig 4F confirms the ChIP text: all five targets enriched in cKO. Recorded also because every Control bar is pinned at exactly 1.0 with no error bar, so the test is against a normalisation constant rather than a measured distribution.
PAIR 1, BODY SIDE. The text claims tumour load was measured relative to body weight.
PAIR 1, PANEL SIDE. Fig 2E plots absolute grams, not a body-weight ratio. Without normalisation the measurement cannot separate tumour burden from a larger animal.
PAIR 2, BODY SIDE. The text asserts the glycolytic targets did not change at the early timepoints — an assertion of measured absence.
PAIR 2, PANEL SIDE. The early and late gene panels are not the same panel. Four genes were never measured at 1 and 3 months, so for those four 'no change' is not a negative result — it is an untested condition. This is the not-significant versus not-tested distinction.
PAIR 3, BODY SIDE. The text puts all four proliferation genes, Axin included, up from one month.
PAIR 3, PANEL SIDE. AXIN2 is not raised at 1 month — it is marginally lower in cKO and carries no significance mark, reaching significance only at 6 months. c-Jun also fails significance at 3 and 6 months, so the continual pattern the Discussion asserts holds for MYC alone.
PAIR 4, BODY SIDE. The therapeutic claim: digoxin downregulates the HIF1alpha targets in the knockout.
PAIR 4, PANEL SIDE. Three of four targets fall under digoxin; PDK1 RISES and carries no significance mark, in the knockout and again in wild-type. The rescue is not uniform across the targets it is claimed for.
PAIR 5, BODY SIDE. The text places the c-Myc elevation after hepatectomy on days 2, 3 and 4.
PAIR 5, PANEL SIDE. Day 2 carries no significance mark; only days 3 and 4 are marked. The day-2 point also has the largest error bar in the series.
PAIR 6, BODY SIDE. The text says the knockout proliferation index kept rising while the control fell — the basis for the claim that WWOX loss removes the termination phase of liver regeneration. THE CITATION IS INHERITED, NOT THE SENTENCE'S OWN: this sentence names no figure, so the snippet is extended backwards to carry the citation of the sentence immediately before it, which is the panel the passage is reading. That inheritance is a reader's inference and is declared as one here rather than presented as the author's pointer.
PAIR 6, PANEL SIDE. The knockout curve does not rise monotonically: it falls at day 4 before rising again at day 7.
The finding that lives only in a panel: florid hepatic steatosis in the knockout on NORMAL chow at 10 months. The running text describes these livers only as poorly differentiated tumours and reports steatosis solely for the high-fat arm. A lipid phenotype on standard diet is the currency of the Iatan lipid question and is invisible to a text-only reader.
PDK1 — the target carrying the muscle-knockout bridge — is measured at exactly one timepoint in this paper, is not significant there, and is then dropped from the later panel. The liver does not reproduce the muscle PDK1 result, and the paper never says so.
The digoxin rescue is demonstrated on a gene subset that excludes the two strongest hits of the experiment it is meant to rescue.
The tumour-incidence chi-square for the digoxin experiment was performed on the CONTROL arm only, where n is 4 in the treated group and the result is not significant. No incidence analysis exists for the knockout arm, whose rescue rests on liver weight and representative images.
The TCGA cohort size is stated three different ways across the paper, and the survival split visible in the figure legend matches neither written number.
The knockout is about 90 percent, not complete, and the paper does not say so in words — expected for an Alb-Cre model measured in whole-liver lysate containing non-parenchymal cells, but it bounds every downstream effect size.
Within one figure the Control/cKO colour mapping inverts between panels — a legibility hazard rather than a data error, since the bars stay labelled.
The high-fat-diet result is solid and its numbers are legible in the panel: incidence 11 of 12 in the knockout against 4 of 18 in control.
CROSS-PAPER OVER-EXTENSION BY LOST QUALIFIER — not a contradiction, and the distinction is the finding. Reference 24 is Iatan 2014, PMID 24871327, which reports lowered HDL-C in the TOTAL-BODY null and separately reports that the sole deletion of Wwox in hepatocytes did NOT change HDL-C in either sex. This Discussion drops the genotype qualifier, writing 'Wwox knockout mouse models' without restriction, inside a paragraph whose entire subject is the liver. The cited result is real; the scope it is carried at is not. That is the failure mode to tag, because a reader checking whether the source says something about HDL will find that it does.
The extent of the hepatectomy is stated as 30 percent in the Methods and Results and as 50 percent in the Figure 7a caption. Both are text and the panel shows no resection extent, so this is an internal textual inconsistency rather than a panel disagreement.
Timing, and the reason the paper's causal direction does not follow from its own data: the proliferation programme moves at 1 month and the glycolytic programme only at 6. The paper nonetheless argues the metabolic change fuels and drives tumour development.
PAIR 1, AND THE METHODS SETTLE IT AGAINST THE RESULTS TEXT. The Results sentence (entries[2]) says tumour load was assessed by liver weight RELATIVE TO BODY WEIGHT; the Methods say, in their own words, that it was grams. So the disagreement is not merely text-versus-panel: the paper contradicts itself in prose, and the Methods side with the panel axis of Fig 2e. This is the locator that removes the charitable reading under which entries[2] was loose wording about a normalised measure.
The same paper DOES normalise liver weight to body weight — in the hepatectomy experiment, whose panel axis is a percentage of body weight. So the absolute-grams measure of Fig 2e and Fig 5c is not a house convention, an unavailable measurement or a limitation of the assay: the authors use both measures in one paper and apply the normalised one only where tumour burden is not the endpoint. That converts entries[3] from 'a normalisation was omitted' into 'a normalisation the authors demonstrably possess was omitted where it would have mattered most'.
SUPPLEMENT PAIR, BODY SIDE. The running text characterises the DEN-free experiment as showing only a 'tendency' of glycolytic-target upregulation, and cites Supplementary Figure S3A for it. 'Tendency' is the vocabulary of a sub-significant drift.
SUPPLEMENT PAIR, PANEL SIDE, AND THE REASON THE SUPPLEMENT HAD TO BE OPENED. S3A does not show a uniform sub-significant drift: two of the five glycolytic targets carry significance marks (PKM2 and PDK1) and three do not (LDHA1, HK2, GLUT1). 'A tendency' understates the two marked genes and overstates the three null ones, so the panel neither simply confirms nor simply contradicts the sentence — it splits it. Recorded also because WWOX itself, reduced to roughly a quarter of control, carries NO significance mark in this panel while the legend defines one.
The design fact that makes S3A worth its own locator: this cohort is DEN-FREE. It is the only place in the paper where HIF1alpha glycolytic targets are measured in Wwox-deleted liver WITHOUT the carcinogen, so it is the only evidence that the glycolytic shift is not purely a tumour-context phenomenon. n=4 per genotype.
THE BOUNDARY ON THE PAPER'S CENTRAL POSITIVE RESULT, VISIBLE ONLY IN THE SUPPLEMENT. The ChIP experiment of Fig 4f — HIF1alpha occupancy on glycolytic promoters, the third side of the hepatic triangle recorded at entries[0] — was run with exactly five promoter primer pairs: PKM, GAPDH, HK2, Glut1 and Aldoa, plus two negative-region controls. PDK1 and LDHA1 are NOT among them. So the promoter-occupancy claim does not extend to the two targets that carry the strongest cross-paper bridges in this repository, and no locator anywhere in the corpus should be read as though it did. The main text names the five genes but the primer roster is what proves the set is closed.
INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION OF PAIR 3, IN A SECOND COHORT. entries[7] found AXIN2 unraised in the DEN model. In the DEN-FREE cohort the same pattern recurs: AXIN2 is marginally LOWER in cKO and carries no significance mark. Recorded with it, because it bounds the proliferative programme rather than extending it: MYC is also unmarked here, so without the carcinogen only JUN and FOS move.
THE CONTROL THAT STRENGTHENS THE HIGH-FAT-DIET RESULT, AND IT EXISTS ONLY IN THE SUPPLEMENT. Under high-fat diet the control and knockout weight curves are superimposed across all 19 sampled points. The HFD tumour difference of Fig 6a (11/12 versus 4/18) therefore cannot be attributed to the knockout becoming more obese on the same diet. This is a genuine negative finding doing positive work, and the running text does not carry it.
THE GLYCOLYTIC TARGET SET IS CONTEXT-DEPENDENT, AND THE PAPER'S FLAGSHIP GENE IS THE ONE THAT DROPS OUT. Under high-fat diet at 11 months PKM2 — the target with the highest ChIP enrichment in Fig 4f and the only one given protein-level confirmation by IHC in Fig 4e — is NOT elevated: it sits slightly below control and carries no mark. What is marked instead is PDK1, LDHA1 and ENO1. So 'HIF1alpha glycolytic targets rise when WWOX is lost' is not a fixed gene set; which members move depends on the metabolic context, and any transfer of this axis that names PKM2 as the invariant readout is unsupported.
THE MOUSE-MODEL COUNTERPART OF THE PAPER'S HUMAN PREMISE, AND IT IS UNMARKED. Wwox mRNA in DEN-induced tumours of CONTROL mice is roughly half that of adjacent parenchyma — but the panel carries no significance mark, on n=3 versus n=3, while the legend defines the asterisk convention. The reduction of WWOX in spontaneous mouse liver tumours is therefore a direction with a plausible effect size and no declared statistic, and should not be cited as an established mouse datum.
The absolute-grams measure recurs in the supplement, and its time course is not monotonic: liver weight separates at 1 month, does NOT separate at 3 months where the knockout is marginally lighter, and separates again at 6 months. A reader taking liver weight as a monotone proxy for accumulating tumour burden is contradicted by the paper's own intermediate timepoint.
Liver injury under high-fat diet: serum ALT is roughly doubled in the knockout at 7 months and carries a significance mark. Recorded with its uncertainty — the knockout error bar spans roughly 45 to 73 against a control bar near 30, so the separation rests on a wide distribution.
A YAP/Hippo-axis readout the main text does not carry: CTGF is elevated roughly 24-fold in the knockout at 1 month and again at 3 months, then returns to control levels at 6 and 10 months. The direction of travel is the opposite of the glycolytic programme, which only separates at 6 and 10 months — so the paper contains two transcriptional programmes with opposite time courses, and this supports the timing argument recorded at entries[24] rather than the paper's own causal ordering.

THE FINDING THIS READING WAS MOST TEMPTED BY, AND IT IS A SECONDARY RESTATEMENT, NOT NEW EVIDENCE. The review states the ITCH-WWOX ubiquitination event as Lys-63-linked with a NON-degradative outcome. Its citation (41) resolves to Abu-Odeh 2014, J Biol Chem 289:8865-8880 = PMID 24550385, which this corpus has ALREADY read at complete_fulltext_read (FTR-20260810-24550385-02). The review therefore adds no independent evidentiary weight for this biology; what it adds is the primary laboratory's own review-level position, dated.
The ONLY occurrence of any degradation word in the whole article body, and it names NO route. Measured over the article prose with the 78-item reference list separated off first: 'proteasom' occurs ZERO times, 'degrad' once - this sentence - and 'Lys-63' once, in the ITCH sentence above. The 2015 review of the primary WWOX laboratory therefore carries a K63 STABILISING ubiquitination and a kinase-triggered 'rapid degradation' side by side, and asserts no endpoint for the second. AUDIT-NOTED (both auditors, independently): the boundary matters and is declared - ref 74's TITLE in the reference list reads 'role of Ack1 in polyubiquitination of tumor suppressor Wwox', so a route WORD exists in the bibliography. It names no chain linkage and no proteasome, and back matter is not the authors' prose about their subject (open item 3 of the receipt contract), so it does not change the finding; it is recorded because a negative measured over a declared window must say what the window excluded.
The review's genotype-phenotype rule is stated at ALLELE level. Read against its own Figure 2B (see the figure locators), three of the six variants it names sit in compound-heterozygous genotypes, so the missense-mild / nonsense-severe correspondence is clean only for the three homozygous rows.
The review's own text supplies the second allele for P47R and thereby the genotype-level confound. AUDIT-CORRECTED twice. (i) The universal is withdrawn: what is supportable is that in this figure P47R is drawn in trans with a truncating allele, and that the two secondary sources this corpus holds - this review and Banne 2021 (PMID 33916893, read by this actor in wave 2) - both place it there; they are not two patients, both trace to Mignot 2015 (PMID 25411445), which this corpus has NOT read. (ii) The text/figure mismatch is a NOTATION discrepancy and is not adjudicated here: the body says 'exon 1 frameshift allele' while Figure 2B labels the allele A16*, an asterisk the caption's own legend defines as a stop codon. A frameshift is often reported at protein level as a truncation, so the two need not describe different alleles; only the unread primary can settle which annotation is the deposited one.
CORROBORATES consolidated baseline   (the WOREE-to-SCAR12 severity spectrum) from a secondary source that names BOTH poles in one sentence and attaches an onset separation to them - 1.5 months at the severe pole against 9-12 months at the milder one. AUDIT-CORRECTED: the snippet was extended to carry the second pole, which the first version's quote did not contain, and the claim that the source 'dates' the WOREE term is withdrawn - it says only 'recently', bounded by this article's 2015-10-23 epub. Secondary corroboration of a claim already held on primary sources adds checkability, not weight.
THE NEGATIVE THAT MATTERS FOR THE CNS MECHANISM, IN THE AUTHORS' OWN WORDS. AUDIT-CORRECTED: the GSK3beta/Tau axis is A mechanistic candidate, not THE one - the same section also offers unstable genome and impaired ROS levels - and it is then explicitly NOT established for the human phenotypes. Any transfer of Tau biology to WWOX-DEE rests on this sentence being ignored.
CORROBORATES consolidated baseline   (WW1-WW2 tandem cooperativity) at the residue level: a single conserved residue in WW2 accounts for its low PPXY affinity, and reverting it restores binding.
CORROBORATES  's other limb - WW1 is the main interacting module - and is a self-summary of the laboratory's own primary work (ref 41 = PMID 24550385, already read here).
THE MECHANISM BEHIND   IS TWO COMPETING MODELS, NOT ONE, AND THE REVIEW DOES NOT CHOOSE. Recorded because a claim that says 'tandem cooperativity' can be read as if the mechanism were settled; the review's own 'Whatever its strategy' sentence follows immediately.
A DATED NEGATIVE, RECORDED WITH ITS DATE ATTACHED (epub 2015-10-23). The enzymatic function of the SDR domain - the domain carrying the reference genotype's missense allele - had no biochemical study of the human protein as of this review. This is the same shape as the E3-ligase negative in the 2014 review by the same senior author, which expired eleven days after its own epub.
Premature death in the severe human phenotype is stated, with no age given, and is compared to the 3-4 week death of Wwox-null mice. Recorded because   and   both turn on survival, and this source gives a direction without a number.
A NEGATIVE ABOUT CANCER RISK, with the authors' own two explanations (short lifespan; further hits required for multistep tumour formation). AUDIT-CORRECTED on scope and on omission: the source says 'these patients', which spans WOREE AND SCAR12 (refs 20, 61-64), not WWOX-DEE alone; and the very next sentence carries a countervailing datum this proposition originally dropped - the CNV-67048 variant of the WWOX locus is correlated with predisposition to lung cancer and gliomas.
The review states its own genotype-phenotype correlation as provisional in the same sentence that proposes it. The qualifier is what a downstream quotation of the rule tends to drop.
AN AUTHOR INFERENCE, REPORTED AS ONE ('suggests'). The SDR domain's critical role is inferred from the severity of truncating alleles, not measured. AUDIT-CORRECTED: the original said the genotypes behind it are 'mostly compound heterozygous', which is an adjective where a count belongs. Counted from the panel and confirmed identically by both auditors: across the nine rows of Figure 2B, 4 are homozygous (i, ii, iv, v), 4 are compound heterozygous (vi, vii, viii, ix) and 1 is unresolved (iii, drawn dotted by the caption's own statement); among the seven rows carrying a deletion or truncation, 4 are compound heterozygous, 2 homozygous and 1 unresolved. Row v is a HOMOZYGOUS truncating row, which is what the withdrawn adjective obscured.
THE Pro-47 DESTABILISATION IS AN EXPECTATION, NOT A MEASUREMENT: no thermodynamic, expression or stability measurement on P47T or P47R appears anywhere in this article. AUDIT-CORRECTED, and this correction runs against the reading's own interest: the original attributed the expectation to the Rosetta model of Figure 3A. The source does not - it grounds it in the residue's conservation and in the 'buckle' role 'revealed by the first structure of the domain' (ref 73, Macias 1996, an EXPERIMENTAL WW-domain structure of another protein), and cites Fig 3A only as illustration. AUDIT-STRENGTHENED in the other direction: the Figure 3A caption drops the body's hedge entirely and states flatly that Pro-47 mutation is 'reducing the stability of WW and consequently its binding to peptide targets'.
The Lde/Lde rat lesion is a frameshift from position 371, which is why the review reads G372R and the rat as pointing at the same C-terminal extension. Recorded because it is the one non-human genetic anchor for the C-terminal tail argument.
EVERY STRUCTURAL MODEL OF WWOX IN THIS ARTICLE IS COMPUTATIONAL, and there is no experimental structure of WWOX in it: the SDR model is a comparative model from template 3rd5 and the WW1 model is built on ITCH's WW3 domain (PDB 4n7f). AUDIT-CORRECTED: the original universal - 'every structural statement rests on computational models' - is falsified inside the same paper, which also carries two experimental structural anchors: the Pro-47 buckle role from the first WW-domain structure (ref 73) and the YXXXK catalytic motif 'confirmed by alanine substitution of residues Tyr-293 and Lys-297'.
THE FIGURE 3 CAPTION DROPS THE QUALIFIER ITS OWN BODY TEXT CARRIES, and the unqualified form is false on the paper's own Figure 2B, which displays P47T, P47R and G372R as point mutations in CNS-disease patients.
The body text's MORE QUALIFIED form of the same statement, quoted beside the caption so the two can be compared without leaving the source. AUDIT-CORRECTED: the original called this form 'correctly qualified' and it is not correct either - by the same counting rule that falsifies the caption, Figure 2B places four further single-residue changes inside the SDR region in CNS-disease patients (H173*, V202*, K297*, W335*). BOTH forms survive only if 'point mutation' silently means 'missense', and that equivocation - not the missing region qualifier - is the actual defect the pair exposes.
THE FIGURE 2 CAPTION GLOSSES ITS 'P' MARKER AS 'proline', AND NO MARKED POSITION IS A PROLINE THE ARTICLE DISCUSSES. AUDIT-CORRECTED, and this was the reading's worst error: the original asserted that the marked positions 'are phosphorylation sites in the paper's own text'. They are not. Searched exhaustively, the article's prose names exactly ONE WWOX phosphorylation site - Tyr-287, phosphorylated by Ack1 - and the only WWOX residues it names anywhere are Pro-47, Tyr-85, Ser-281, Tyr-287, Tyr-293 and Lys-297. The identification of the other marked positions came from this reader's background knowledge and not from the source, which is an undeclared DEFAULT_FROM_TEXTBOOK and is withdrawn. What survives, measured: see the Figure 2A attestation.
THE FIGURE 2 CAPTION'S BLANKET SOURCE ATTRIBUTION IS INCONSISTENT WITH ITS OWN PER-PATIENT LIST. Reference 59 is Nunez et al. 2006, 'WWOX protein expression in normal human tissues', a normal-tissue expression study with no patients; the per-patient attributions that follow in the same caption name refs 20, 61, 62, 63, 65 and 75, and never 59. Verified on the rendered PDF page 3 as well as in the HTML, because a digit is exactly what an extraction can damage.
Figure 1's caption asserts the GSK3beta-Tau arm without a qualifier, in the same caption that marks ATM and p73 as unknown for the same phenotype. Quoted so the asymmetry can be checked against the panel.
The caption's own hedge, applied to ATM and p73 only.
READ FROM THE PIXELS AT 8x, AND THIS IS THE READING'S PRINCIPAL GENOTYPE-LEVEL FINDING. In Figure 2B the patient rows are drawn as two allele bars each. Row vi carries a solid blue bar truncating at a tick near residue 16 labelled A16*, and a full-length GREEN bar carrying a tick at approximately residue 47 labelled P47R. P47R is therefore in trans with a truncating exon-1 allele in this figure, never alone. The phenotype annotation for row vi is not a single letter: it is 'S' and 'W' separated by a double-headed arrow, the only row in the panel so marked, while the caption defines only 'S stands for SCAR12, and W stands for WOREE' and never explains the arrow.
THE ALLELE-LEVEL RULE AGAINST THE GENOTYPE-LEVEL PANEL, COUNTED. Of the six variants the running text names in its genotype-phenotype sentence, Figure 2B draws THREE as homozygous - P47T (row i, tick crossing both bars, phenotype S), G372R (row ii, tick crossing both bars, phenotype S) and R54* (row iv, tick crossing both bars, phenotype W) - and THREE in trans with a different second allele: P47R with A16* (row vi), W335* with the Exon5del/H173* allele (row viii, phenotype W) and K297* with Exon1-9del (row ix, phenotype W).
MEASURED FROM THE PIXELS, AND THE ONE POINT ON WHICH THE TWO BLIND AUDITORS DISAGREED - ADJUDICATED HERE AGAINST ONE OF THEM. Figure 2A carries FOUR marker stalks, not the three this reading first counted: the leftmost box is a doubled trapezoid. Calibrating on the protein bar's own ends (x=68 -> residue 1, x=2121 -> residue 414), the stalks sit at residues 12.3, 14.3, 33.2 and 286.9. One auditor placed the left pair at 12.1 and 14.1 and said they do NOT land on the residue-16 boundary tick; the other placed them at 13.4 and 15.4 and accepted 'the residue-16 tick'. This measurement agrees with the first: the tick for residue 16 falls at x=142.6 and both left stalks are 8 and 19 px to its left, so they sit inside the beige pre-WW1 block and not on the tick. CONSEQUENCE: of the four marked positions, exactly one (286.9) corresponds to a residue the article identifies at all - Tyr-287, its single named phosphorylation site - and three are unexplained by the text in any way. Pro-47, the only proline the article discusses and the site of both WW1 CNS missense alleles, carries no marker at all, while the caption glosses the marker as 'proline'.
THE PANEL SAYS MORE THAN THE TEXT ALLOWS, AND MARKS ITS UNCERTAINTY ASYMMETRICALLY. Figure 1's neurodegeneration node lists 'Tau1, GSK3beta, ATM, p73 ?' with a single question mark following p73. AUDIT-NOTED: from the pixels alone a trailing '?' could be read as scoping the whole list; it is the CAPTION that ties the hedge to ATM and p73 specifically, so the asymmetry is established by caption and panel together and not by the panel alone. The body text states that whether the GSK3beta/Tau effectors matter for SCAR12 and WOREE is 'still unknown', so the unhedged half of the node is not better established than the hedged half.
Figure 3 is two ribbon models and no experimental structure. Panel A is a WW1 model with Pro-47 drawn in magenta sticks inside the fold and a peptide ligand in white; panel B is the SDR comparative model in two views, the left carrying cancer-mutation positions as spheres and the right the single CNS mutation G372R. Attested so that no structural statement carried out of this paper is mistaken for a measurement. AUDIT-NOTED: the phrase 'in the core' was the caption's language and is not adjudicable from a single rendered view; the attestation now says only where the residue sits in the render.

The transcriptome is GSE126075 from Kosla 2019, an shRNA knockdown in H9-derived human neural progenitors. So the paper's three lines of evidence come from three unrelated systems — one human fetus carrying p.Arg264Ter, a rat carrying a 13-bp exon-9 deletion, and an shRNA knockdown in an embryonic-stem-cell-derived line — and none of the molecular work was done in the genotype the paper is about. That is a legitimate design, but it means the transcriptomic figure must never be weighted as independent replication of the histology, and any downstream use of TUBA1A/TUBB3 has to carry the system it came from.
🔴 THE SIGNIFICANCE AXIS OF THE ONLY MOLECULAR FIGURE CANNOT BE MAPPED ONTO ANY STATED THRESHOLD. The y-axis of both volcano plots is labelled '-Log10 adjusted differential value p'. Read literally, the dashed threshold line sits at about 0.83 on that axis, i.e. p around 0.15, and the most extreme point in either panel reaches about 1.4, i.e. p around 0.04 — meaning that across 9,404 and 9,318 variables not one gene would reach p<0.04. That is not a credible p-value distribution for a transcriptome comparison. The Methods do not resolve it: they say significance came from the NOISeq-sim algorithm, and NOISeq's statistic is a PROBABILITY of differential expression whose conventional cut is 0.8, not a p-value — and 0.8 is almost exactly where the threshold line sits. But values above 1.0 appear in both panels, which a probability cannot take. So the axis is consistent with neither reading, and the Discussion's phrase 'significantly reduced expression' rests on a criterion that the paper does not let a reader reconstruct. This is a PREMISE_TAG on everything downstream of the tubulin result, not a refutation of it.
🔴 THE ABSTRACT ATTRIBUTES THE TRANSCRIPTOMIC FINDING TO PROGENITORS; THE PANEL SHOWS IT IN NEURONS. The abstract's sentence is 'Transcriptomic analyses of Wwox-depleted human neural progenitor cells showed an impaired expression of a number of neuronal migration-related genes encoding for tubulins, kinesins and associated proteins'. The Results sentence quoted here is correct and says neurons. Figure 4 settles which is which: in the left panel (progenitors) the labelled migration genes sit in the grey non-significant cloud or in green (fold-change only) — TUBB3, DNM1, TUBB6, MAP6 and TUBA1B are all below the threshold line — while in the right panel (neurons) the same names sit in red, above threshold and at log2 fold changes between roughly -1.5 and -4.5. The finding is differentiation-dependent, and the abstract is the sentence most readers will carry away.
THE FOLD CHANGES THE TEXT CLAIMS ARE CONSISTENT WITH THE PANEL, AND THIS IS RECORDED AS A POSITIVE VERIFICATION RATHER THAN LEFT SILENT. >15-fold is log2 -3.91 and >3-fold is log2 -1.58; in the neurons panel the TUBB3 leader line reaches the far-left extreme of the red cluster near log2 -3.6 to -4, and TUBB2B, MAP2 and the KIF5 family point into the -1.2 to -1.8 band, matching the '2-3-fold' and '3-fold' the text gives for them. The quantitative claims survive inspection; what does not survive is the significance criterion behind them (entry 11).
🔴 THE PROTEIN-LEVEL TEST OF THE PAPER'S CENTRAL MOLECULAR CLAIM WAS DONE, WAS NEGATIVE, AND IS CONFINED TO ONE HALF-SENTENCE THAT THE DISCUSSION NEVER REPEATS. A greater-than-tenfold mRNA reduction was checked at the protein level in the actual WWOX-deficient human brain and the reduction was slight and not significant. The Discussion then says only 'This showed a significantly reduced expression of several tubulins, microtubule-associated proteins and microtubule motor kinesins', with no mention of the protein result. This is the same asymmetry recorded as DL-BIO-085: transcript abundance is not a readout of protein, and protein abundance is not a readout of function. Here the paper had the protein measurement and the negative did not travel.
🔴 FIGURE 2A LABELS THE CORTICAL LAYERS ONLY ON THE CONTROL, SO THE ABNORMAL SPECIMEN'S LAYER IDENTIFICATION IS ASSERTED RATHER THAN SHOWN. The claim of the paper's sole human experiment is that the external granular layer has migrated INTO the molecular layer. Verifying that requires knowing which band is which in the patient section — and it is exactly the patient section that carries no annotation. The control panel carries ML, EGL and CG with tick marks at the tissue edge; the patient panel carries none, in either magnification. The control and patient fields are also not matched in orientation, which limits a morphological comparison independently of the labelling.
🔴 FIGURE 1B SHOWS FOUR SANGER TRACES WHILE ITS CAPTION NAMES THREE INDIVIDUALS, AND NO TRACE IS LABELLED. The caption reads 'Electropherograms of carrier parents and index case (II.1)' — two parents plus one proband. The panel shows four sequence rows. The fourth is most plausibly the fetus II.3, whose prenatal Sanger result the Results section reports, but the panel does not say so and carries no per-trace identification at all, so which trace belongs to whom is not recoverable from the figure. WHAT I CANNOT CALL AT THIS RESOLUTION, DECLARED RATHER THAN GUESSED: the boxed base of the first trace is called 'N' while its chromatogram looks single-peaked like the homozygous fourth trace, where the second and third traces show the clear double peaks of heterozygotes. Panel B occupies roughly 450x290 native pixels; that is not enough to decide whether a minor allele peak is present, and upscaling is interpolation, not evidence. Recorded as an unresolved observation, not a finding.
THE RAT ALLELE, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS NOT THE SAME LESION AS THE HUMAN ONE AND THE PAPER READS THE TWO AS EQUIVALENT. The lde/lde rat carries a 13-bp exon-9 deletion truncating the Wwox C-terminus; the family carries a stop at codon 264. Both are C-terminal truncations, which is the basis for reading the rat as a model of this family — but exon 9 is well downstream of residue 264, so the rat retains more of the protein than the human variant would if it escapes NMD. The cross-species argument is reasonable and is not the same as identity.
THE RAT EXPERIMENTS ARE n=3 PER GENOTYPE, STATED ONCE IN THE METHODS AND NOWHERE IN THE RESULTS. Every asterisk in panels 3E, 3G, 3H and 3J — including the eight significant zones of entry 4 — rests on three animals per group compared by Student's t-test, with no correction for the ten zones tested per panel. The effect in zone 2 is large enough that this is unlikely to explain it away; the smaller markers at zones 4, 9 and 10 are a different matter. Recorded so that the eight-of-ten count is never quoted without its n.
WHY THIS PAPER WAS WORTH THE UNREAD-PREMISE CLOSURE, IN THE AUTHORS' OWN FRAMING. Before this study nobody had looked at cerebral cortex development under a pathogenic WWOX variant, and the neuropathology of WOREE had never been examined. Whatever the qualifications recorded above, the human fetal histology and the perinatal rat cortex are the paper's genuine first, and they are the reason FT-002 sat at HIGH priority while being cited in the meta layer without ever having been read.
THE CORTICAL WALL IS NOT THINNER, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS A MIGRATION PHENOTYPE RATHER THAN A GROWTH ONE. Panel 3E carries no significance marker and the text agrees. The point is worth its own entry because the negative is load-bearing in the opposite direction from usual: if the mutant cortex were simply smaller, a redistribution of birth-dated neurons across ten equal zones could be an artefact of dividing a shorter wall. It is not smaller — if anything the mutant mean is slightly higher — so the zone-by-zone redistribution in panel 3J is about where cells are, not about how much wall there is to divide.
🔴 FIGURE 4 ITSELF, WHICH IS BOTH THE TARGET OF ENTRY 11 AND THE PANEL THAT SEPARATES PROGENITORS FROM NEURONS. Two volcano plots share a y-axis labelled '-Log10 adjusted differential value p' whose printed gridlines are 0.3, 0.5 and 1.0 with non-uniform spacing — the gap from 1.0 to 0.5 stands to the gap from 0.5 to 0.3 as 1.37 to 1, against the 1.36 to 1 that a logarithmic axis predicts and the 1.5 to 1 a linear one would give, so the axis is itself log-scaled in a quantity that is already a negative logarithm. The dashed significance line sits near 0.83 and the highest points reach about 1.4. The left panel is the progenitor comparison and the right the neuron comparison, and the LABELLED MIGRATION GENES CHANGE COLOUR BETWEEN THEM: in the left panel TUBB3, DNM1, TUBB6, MAP6, TUBGCP6 and TUBA1B sit in the grey non-significant cloud or in green below the threshold line, and TUBA1A sits in blue; in the right panel the same names sit in red above the line, with leader lines reaching log2 fold changes from about -1.2 to -4.5. Total variables printed beneath the panels: 9,404 left and 9,318 right.

The text asserts no significant difference in locomotor velocity or distance; panels 4D and 4E each carry an asterisk, and the caption defines asterisk as p < 0.05 while using ns freely in the same figure. Panel 7C prints 0.2000 above the WT-versus-KO bracket for average spikes per day, with no asterisk and no ns, at n = 5 per group; the running text calls the same comparison a significant elevation. The SWD panel 7E is unaffected and solid: **** for WT-vs-KO and KO-vs-HD, ns for WT-vs-HD. Read from a fingerprinted raster image, never from a text layer — the 0.2000 is printed pixels, not extracted characters.
The sentence panel 7C contradicts.
The Figure 7 caption, which fixes the significance scale and also corrects the cohort size I had estimated from the plotted points as about 3.
THE DOSE-DEPENDENCE OF MYELINATION IS NEVER QUANTIFIED. Three separate panels show treated-animal myelination and none measures it: Figure 6F, Supplementary S7I and Supplementary S8G are all representative images without graphs or statistics. The only MBP quantification in the paper, Figure 6E, compares WT against KO with no treated arm. This claim was withdrawn earlier today on the false premise that S7I held the quantification, and is reinstated on what the panel shows.
The sentence that cites S7I as if it carried the quantification — the sentence that caused the mistaken withdrawal.
Neuroinflammation IS quantified, and the low dose is significantly worse than wild type on astrogliosis while the high dose is not — one more instance of LD failing where HD succeeds. S7F and S7H contain no untreated-KO arm, so within S7 the claimed reduction has no baseline; S8I supplies it.
The untreated-KO baseline missing from S7 exists in S8I, and it supports the paper's astrogliosis claim: GFAP-positive cells WT about 5, KO about 44, treated at P5 back to about 5, with *** for WT-vs-KO and ns for WT-vs-treated.
THE P0-P5 WINDOW, VERIFIED AGAINST ITS PANEL rather than taken from running text. Treatment at any point P1-P5 gives survival to 300 days, and weight and glucose at P14 are ns against wild type across all five timepoints. What the panels add: the 300-day plot shows only P1 and P5; P2, P3 and P4 appear solely in the 40-day panel, and P3 is an n=3 arm that lost animals.
The survival threshold, stated in plain text and no longer read off a curve: the low dose does not produce animals that reach three months.
THE SURVIVAL THRESHOLD HAS NO MEASURED EXPRESSION DIFFERENCE BEHIND IT. Two doses differing 2.1-fold are statistically indistinguishable in vector genomes and mRNA across four brain regions — seven of eight comparisons ns, the exception being hippocampal DNA — while producing opposite survival outcomes. Cerebellum stays below wild type at both doses; the hippocampal KO lane reads 1.1 where the other three blots read 0.02, 0.03 and 0.08.
The paper's own explanation for that mismatch, credited and unverifiable here: expression predicts survival within each dose group, which lets group means overlap while outcomes diverge. It is a post-hoc comparison of survivors against non-survivors, i.e. selection-conditioned, and it rests on supplementary panels S5A-S5D.
Four survival doses exist across two figures and no single figure displays them: at 4E10 and 8E10 no treated arm survives, at 1.23E11 death by about 90 days, at 2.63E11 a plateau. The threshold is therefore not an artefact of comparing two doses.
WPRE removal did not lower transgene burden — it made it predictable and required a six-fold dose increase to recover efficacy. Protein without WPRE at 2E10 sits at or below wild type.
The Methods settle from their own side the correction I had to make to my Figure 1 criticism: the promoter comparison used WPRE-bearing constructs throughout, so its 4E10 is not the 4E10 of Figures 2 and 3.
The MBP vector produced essentially no detectable WWOX, so the oligodendrocyte question raised by PMID 34747138 is unanswered by this experiment rather than answered negatively.
The construct is neuron-specific but not CNS-confined: after neonatal ICV, WWOX protein reaches the sciatic nerve of high-dose animals while the liver stays negative. A biodistribution fact any safety assessment needs, obtained by the sciatic-nerve and spinal-cord dissection the Methods describe.
S6 QUALIFIES THE PNS LOCATOR ABOVE RATHER THAN CONFIRMING IT CLEANLY. The sciatic-nerve result is a blot with no quantification and visibly variable band intensity across seven high-dose animals; the panel the caption pairs it with contains four wild-type lanes rather than a WT-versus-treated comparison. The liver result is clean: treated lanes sit in the same 0.03-0.1 range as untreated Wwox-null lanes, i.e. at background for an animal with no WWOX. Cerebellum remains below wild type at P300, confirming from a second timepoint what Figure 5L showed at P30.
Injection technique changed between the two papers, a declared methodological upgrade: stereotaxic here, free-hand in PMID 34747138.
Blinding is declared more weakly than in the 2021 paper, which stated it unconditionally.
Declared commercial interest, absent from the 2021 paper, which stated no conflict of interest. Recorded as context for the two text-versus-panel contradictions above, not as an argument against the data.
Transduction efficiency, correcting a number I had carried over from the 2021 paper.
S1 does not establish the neuron specificity claimed for the GFP control by colocalisation: panel D contains DAPI and SynI-EGFP only, without a neuronal marker. The promoter comparison itself is qualitative and shows weak MBP-driven WWOX in cerebellum, while corpus-callosum WWOX signal remains visible under several promoters.
S2 contains an internal sample-size conflict: the plotted CBA-treated survival legend says n=5, whereas its caption says n=4. The curve also shows partial rather than full survival rescue, ending near 50 percent by day 30.
S3 confirms that WPRE, not dose alone, drives the high and spatially diffuse expression state. At each matched dose WPRE produces much more protein; without WPRE, doubling 2E10 to 4E10 significantly raises the percentage of positive neurons only in cortex, not hippocampus or cerebellum.
The motor rescue in S4 is dose-graded rather than binary: high dose is indistinguishable from wild type, low dose remains intermediate, and low versus high dose is significant. Fertility is presented from only about three plotted observations per group and without an untreated-KO comparator.
S5 makes the expression-survival argument selection-conditioned: the P90 blots explicitly mark one HD and three LD animals as dead, so the later dose comparison is necessarily made among survivors. It also shows durable regional overexpression, with the P300 HD blot labelled 8.2-fold cortex, 10.7-fold hippocampus, 5.6-fold midbrain and 1.4-fold cerebellum relative to WT.
